results.title: [2407.14743] Denoising Long- and Short-term Interests for Sequential Recommendation

item.text: {"text":"Recent work supports separating persistent preferences from current intent. [Denoising Long- and Short-term Interests (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.14743) uses session-level interest extraction/evolution for long-term modeling and contrastive augmentation to reduce short-term behavioral noise. [Hierarchical preference modeling (2025)](https://journal.hep.com.cn/fcs/EN/10.1007/s11704-025-41181-y) combines multiple long-term interest vectors, short-term self-attention, similarity-based matching, and time encoding. [Multi-Scale Transformers (2026)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0306457325002596) separates persistent preferences across patches from transient interests within patches, with adaptive masking to reduce redundancy. These provide architectural precedents; they do not establish that isolated purchases indicate dissatisfaction.\n\nFor complementary next purchases, [TGCL4SR (2024)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/28789) learns global temporal item transitions alongside a local Transformer with time-interval embeddings—useful machinery for learning directional associations beyond item similarity, although transitions alone do not establish complementarity. [CURE (2026)](https://doi.org/10.1109/TBDATA.2026.3679591) proposes front-door adjustment using long-term and periodic interests as mediators, but assumes those mediators are unaffected by confounders and uses LLM-generated interest labels; its causal interpretation is assumption-dependent and its supervision is unsuitable here. Practical synthesis: retain a causal SASRec branch for current intent, add several persistent-interest vectors pooled from prefix histories, and gate their scores using recurrence and elapsed time. Add a separate directional transition scorer trained exclusively on training histories. Treat recurrence as evidence of persistence and isolated events as uncertain; purchases provide neither satisfaction labels nor observed conformity traits. This is a proposed adaptation, requiring validation on the matched benchmark."}
